topics.topic_label: AI safety institutes (CAISI 40+ assessments incl. classified, UK AISI Microsoft partnership, NIST TRAINS, Apollo DC office)

Content provenance & copyright (Article 50 went live on 2 August so AI-generated or manipulated content must carry machine-readable labels - and on the same front page TIME is caught serving AI crawlers a different site with advertising embedded in the text models ingest, Meta ran ads containing AI-generated CSAM, and Grokipedia is found to have silently stopped reviewing edits in April while still presenting as live)

AI vendor trust friction (the dominant thread under Cloudflare OS is lock-in anxiety rather than architecture, and the second-loudest attacks the 'OS' branding as invented marketing language; Meta's discount for training rights comes with small print documented as appearing after free credits were granted; DeepSeek signals a significant price rise without publishing rates; and a benchmark board is caught changing its own numbers between two page loads)

Content provenance & training-data copyright (Oracle bars AI-generated code from OpenJDK, read on HN as legal positioning — Oracle wants to preserve its ability to sue over AI-washed proprietary code, which it cannot do while accepting unprovenanced AI contributions; the EU AI Act's machine-readable content-marking duty is now operative and is an engineering task, not a legal one)

AI vendor trust friction (the detail that reframes the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident is that OpenAI only learned it had caused the breach when it asked HF to revoke credentials and was told they already had been; a commenter screenshots the Artificial Analysis leaderboard flipping both order and scores between two page loads with identical chart copy; and HN reads OpenAI's cyber post as pre-emptive positioning rather than disclosure)
